title: Diagnosing a High Electric Bill with Home Energy Monitoring (This Old House)

summary: This This Old House episode follows a multi-tenant house facing a winter spike in electric bills. The team inventories the building’s electric loads, reviews the service and meter configuration, and uses analog meters to gauge real-time usage. They install a home energy monitoring system with current transformers (CTS) to isolate and track power draw across circuits, then perform controlled load-off tests to verify impact. After a two-month follow-up, they correlate real-time data with the utility bill to identify three major energy culprits—the mini-split heat pump, the well pump, and the electric water heater—and discuss practical savings (e.g., a hybrid heat-pump water heater) and the potential role of solar. The episode demonstrates a data-driven approach to diagnosing and reducing electricity costs in a multifamily home.

sections.title: Problem framing and house-load context
sections.description: Host frames common reasons for a high bill and introduces a case with an older house that has added electrical loads like EV charging and a mini-split; sets a plan to diagnose by observing loads and taking measurements.

sections.title: Basement panel layout and meter configuration
sections.description: Discussion and on-site notes identify multiple panels in the basement (including a kitchen panel and a garage subpanel) and the presence of two exterior meters with a separate third-floor meter.

sections.title: Meter observation and test plan
sections.description: The team observes the spinning analog meters to gauge real-time usage and plans to test by turning off large loads to see the effect on the meter.

sections.title: Energy monitor system overview
sections.description: Owner explains the monitor’s components (the brain unit and the monitor), how current transformers wrap around main feeders and circuits, and how power and network connectivity are established.

sections.title: Install sequence and testing readiness
sections.description: Plan and initial steps for mounting transformers, orienting CTs, and preparing to power the system back up after installation.

sections.title: Two-month follow-up: data-driven culprit identification
concepts: culprits: mini split, well pump, water heater
sections.description: Two months after installation, the team reviews live data and historical views, identifying three major energy consumers and discussing potential savings (e.g., hybrid water heater) and solar as a long-term option, with emphasis on data correlation to the bill.

sections.title: Closing and resources
sections.description: Host closes the segment and points viewers to additional This Old House content and subscription options.
